title.en: Prime Minister, Council of Ministers and Parliament

text.en: The President signs, but the real work of governing is done by a team led by the Prime Minister. That team answers to the Lok Sabha, the House elected by the people.

The Prime Minister heads the Council of Ministers, which aids and advises the President under Article 74.
India follows the Westminster model, so the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha is appointed Prime Minister.
If no party has a majority, the President may call a leader who can form a ministry.
Other ministers are appointed on the PM's advice, and a non-member can be a minister if elected to Parliament within six months.
Ministers are classified as Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers.
The Cabinet, the senior ministers, takes key decisions such as defence, finance, external affairs and home.
The Council of Ministers is limited to 15 percent of the strength of the Lok Sabha.
Ministers are individually and collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
The Prime Minister distributes portfolios, presides over Cabinet, supervises ministers and links the President and the Council.
Parliament has three parts, the President, the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha, so it is bicameral.
The Rajya Sabha has 250 members, 238 representing states and Union Territories and 12 nominated, and is a permanent house with a six-year term.
One third of its members retire every two years, and its members must be 30 years old.
The Lok Sabha has 543 elected members, 530 from states and 13 from Union Territories, with a five-year term and minimum age 25.
Rajya Sabha members are elected by MLAs by single transferable vote, so the election is indirect.

problem.en: Explain how the Prime Minister is appointed and what he does.

text.en: The President appoints the leader of the majority party in Lok Sabha.
He chooses ministers and distributes portfolios.

why.en: Ministers are appointed on his advice.

text.en: He presides over the Cabinet and links the Council with the President.

why.en: He also represents India at SAARC and Commonwealth meetings.

prompt.en: Compare Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

requiredIdeas.en: Lok Sabha 543 elected, five-year term, age 25
Rajya Sabha 250, permanent, six-year term, age 30

commonMisconceptions.en: Saying the Rajya Sabha can be dissolved

points.en: PM: leader of the Lok Sabha majority, Westminster model.
Ministers: Cabinet, State, Deputy; limited to 15 percent of Lok Sabha.
Parliament: President, Rajya Sabha, Lok Sabha.
Rajya Sabha permanent, Lok Sabha five years.
